title: A large retailer reports privacy-request completion and denial as separate control stages
source_unit: Walmart corporate California privacy-rights metrics for 2025 requests, updated June 18, 2026
geography: California residents submitting CCPA requests to Walmart

observations.period: 2025 calendar year; company metrics updated June 18, 2026

denominator.unit: reported California privacy-rights request rows across access, deletion, and sale-opt-out categories; categories are not a unique-person denominator

individual_data_effect.unit: missing person-level deletion verification, residual data, trust, switching, or wellbeing

observations.method: Walmart's published CCPA metrics; received, completed, denied, and median completion time are preserved as separate administrative stages. The company says identity or authorization verification is required and lists valid exemptions as possible denial reasons.
observations.uncertainty: The metrics are company-reported aggregates and do not establish whether a completed request removed all relevant data, whether an individual received a satisfactory explanation, whether data reappeared, or whether the person changed provider behavior.
observations.subgroup: California residents and authorized agents submitting privacy requests to Walmart; the page does not provide demographic or socioeconomic subgroup outcomes.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high completion count can show administrative capacity while denial, verification, exemption, or residual-data rules still leave unequal practical control; an opt-out completion is not the same as deletion.

related_sources.claim: California's DROP creates a separate multi-broker deletion route with status tracking and a 45-day processing rule.

boundary: This record adds an account-holder administrative completion stage to the platform/data-control lane: requests, verification/denial, completion, and timing are visible in a named company report. It does not verify individual deletion, residual data, adequacy, trust, switching, or wellbeing, and it does not pool Walmart's request universe with California DROP or other companies.
